each demo request. An instance is over when a submission is correct or when the attempt
cap is reached, and one that ends unsolved costs the whole budget, 16, however
many submissions and demo requests it used. Feedback on a submission is only
correct/incorrect. There is no way to abandon an instance, and finish is refused until

Treat target color 0 as demo-validated for this family.", path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T04:12:06.381698+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T04:19:55.701095+00:00', version=3), HarnessEntry(id='periodic_arc_grid_extend_colored_line_residue_pattern', kind='memory', title='Periodic ARC grid: extend colored line residue pattern', content='For this task family, a sparse set of colored straight lines encodes a periodic color pattern; complete zeros by repeating the pattern in the line-normal/phase coordinate. Infer the SMALLEST period p for which all clues at the same phase are consistent, then propagate the observed colors across the grid. For diagonal line clues slope +1, phase is (column-row) mod p; the output is the corresponding periodic diagonal-band tiling. Demonstrations: 13x13 horizontal stripes produced row period 7; 16x16 diagonal clues period 5; 26x26 diagonal clues period 8; 14x14 diagonal clues period 6. Preserve clue lines and fill missing residue classes consistently. Avoid guessing period from number of distinct colors alone: minimum compatible period worked for the solved horizontal case.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T02:09:30.340291+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T02:09:30.340312+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_grid_cells_with_uniform_marker_corners', kind='memory', title='ARC grid of matching four-corner marker cells', content='For ARC inputs made of large uniform rectangular tiles separated by a one-cell lattice of a different base/separator color, with sparse marker colors at lattice intersections, read the intersection colors as a vertex matrix. For every adjacent 2x2 vertex group, output its shared color only when all four corners match; otherwise use the tile/interior background color. Ignore the separator color as a marker. Then crop the result to the smallest bounding rectangle containing all shared-color cells; retain background-valued gaps inside that box, and omit all-background margins outside. Example: a 27x19 demo with background 8, marker 1 in cell (0,0), and marker 3 in (2,1) produced [[1,8],[8,8],[8,3]], cropping away one all-background top row. Confirmed on task-f63064b0: a lattice with 3x4 interior tiles of 7, matching-corner cells were 4 at (0,0), 2 at (0,2), 8 at (2,0), 1 at (2,2) and (3,2); cropped output [[4,7,2],[7,7,7],[8,7,1],[7,7,1]] was correct. Earlier evidence: a 5x5 vertex lattice with interior 9 and markers 7/8 produced 4x4 output where only cells with four matching corners retained the marker; a 4x4 vertex lattice on separator 2 / interior 0 produced [[0,7,7],[0,0,0],[7,0,8]].

Additional confirmation (task-f63064b0, 2026-10-21): On a 21x28 grid with interior/background 1, separator lattice color 7, horizontal lattice rows 5 and 16, and vertical lattice columns 1, 13, and 25, all six intersections were marker 5. The output was [[5,5]]: one output cell per adjacent pair of horizontal/vertical lattice coordinates, with each cell taking the shared color iff all four corner markers agree; crop away all-background output margins. This also confirms rectangular, non-square lattice spacing is fine.

Additional confirmation (task-f63064b0, 2026-10-21): A 19x28 lattice with 3 output tile rows and 6 candidate tile columns had separator color 5, interior background 0, and marker intersections at columns 9,13,21,25 on lattice rows 0,6,12,18. The missing column-17 intersections must not be skipped: build every adjacent lattice cell from the first through last marker column, retaining all-background cells in gaps. The cropped correct output was [[7,0,0,2],[0,0,0,0],[6,0,0,0]]. This confirms cropping to the bounding box of non-background output cells while preserving empty rows/columns inside that box.', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T03:34:48.972879+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T03:44:04.413280+00:00', version=4), HarnessEntry(id='periodic_arc_grid_phase_selection_examples_and_caution', kind='memory', title='Periodic ARC grid: phase selection examples and caution', content='Observed examples for the periodic-line ARC task: output is a 2D periodic tiling where color is constant along each marked diagonal (down-right lines; class c-r mod p), or each full-width horizontal stripe (class row mod p). The earlier guessed p=5 was incorrect, so use minimum compatible p, not unique-color-count+1. Diagonal demos confirmed periods 5 (14/16 grids), 6 (14 grid), and 8 (26 grid), from congruence of line offsets. If some residue classes lack a direct clue, do not assume a new color; examples fill a missing adjacent phase with the same color as a neighboring phase (e.g., p=5 demo had phase sequence [5,3,3,8,4]).', path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T02:09:49.203914+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T02:09:49.203928+00:00', version=1), HarnessEntry(id='arc_l_shaped_9_marker_selects_matching_object_to_recolor', kind='memory', title='ARC L-shaped 9 marker selects matching object to recolor', content="Validated ARC rule from task-63ec3175 demos and test. Color 9 may form a long L-shaped corner marker; find repeated identical non-background object shapes. Recolor one member of a matching pair to color 9, leaving its duplicate unchanged. Demonstration evidence: (1) marker with arms east+south, identical 6-cell color-7 shapes NW and SE of elbow; NW copy changes to 9. (2) marker with arms north+west, identical vertical 2-cell color-5 shapes NW and SE; SE copy changes to 9. In the solved test, marker arms north+east; identical 7-cell shapes color 5 at rows 0-2 cols 24-27 and color 6 at rows 6-8 cols 24-27; lower (south-of-elbow) copy changed from 6 to 9. Thus the selected copy is often on the side opposite the vertical arm direction; when duplicates straddle both marker axes it is in the diagonally open quadrant. Do not require the selected shape to have the same original color as its duplicate. A separate demo variant had two small 3-cell 9 Ls and a matching 3-cell color-1 L recolored to color 5 (rather than 9), so use the observed surrounding template/color relationship if marker consists of small L objects rather than one long frame. Preserve all other cells.

Additional solved task-63ec3175 instance (12x14, background 0): color-6 long L frame has elbow r4c4, arms north and west. Two identical vertical 2-cell color-8 objects at {(1,1),(2,1)} (NW) and {(6,5),(7,5)} (SE). Recolor the SE object to frame color 6, leaving NW unchanged and all other cells intact; this output was confirmed correct. This confirms the long-frame color is the recolor destination even when it is not 9, and for an NW/SE pair with a north+west frame the SE copy is selected. For this orientation, marker-frame arms north+west -> choose the matching object SE of the elbow. Keep the distinction between long L frame and small standalone L marker patterns; don't infer the transformation based only on color 9.

Additional solved recurrence (12x19, background 6; output confirmed correct after one wrong submission): a color-9 long L frame occupied row 7, cols 0-4, plus col 4, rows 7-11 (arms east and south). Two identical 8-cell shapes were at rows 9-11, cols 0-2 (color 0) and cols 8-10 (color 5); a separate color-5 singleton at r6c10 remained unchanged. Correctly recolor the right-hand color-5 shape at rows 9-11, cols 8-10 to 9, leaving the left-hand color-0 copy unchanged. Recoloring the left copy to 9 was explicitly submitted and incorrect. This instance shows that arm orientation alone / a guessed open-quadrant rule is insufficient when the matching copies do not straddle both axes; preserve exact recurrence evidence and avoid assuming the left copy is selected just because it lies west of the vertical arm. The long-frame color is still the destination color.

Further confirmed 17x26 recurrence, showing frame color need not be 9: bg1; thin color5 frame has elbow r13c17 and arms east+south. Two exact matching 13-cell shapes (a 2x7 bar missing bottom-right) are color0 at rows12-13 cols10-16 (NW) and color2 at rows15-16 cols19-25 (SE). Recolor NW copy to frame color5; confirmed correct. A decoy repeated horizontal 2-cell color3 pair also straddled north/south west of the frame, but recoloring its NW member was incorrect. First identify the actual exact matching pair straddling opposite quadrants on both frame axes; do not act on any repeated shape indiscriminately. After selecting the correct pair, color the member in the open diagonal quadrant (opposite both frame arms) with the frame color.

Three further demonstrations reinforce orientation-independent frame color: a color5 frame with arms north+east selects SW copy from color8/color2 matching 3-cell Ls; a color1 frame with arms south+west selects NE color6 copy from a matching 2-cell bar pair; a color6 frame with arms west+south selects NE color5 triangle copy. Treat a thin long L frame as the selection marker regardless of its color; distinguish it from small standalone L marker patterns, where color mapping may differ.

Confirmed 21x20 task-63ec3175 recurrence: bg3; long color6 L frame has elbow r15c7, arms west and south (horizontal row15 c0-7; vertical c7 rows15-20). Two identical 7-cell shapes: color1 at {(5,8),(6,8),(6,9),(6,10),(7,8),(7,9),(8,8)} (NE/open quadrant) and color8 at {(17,0),(18,0),(18,1),(18,2),(19,0),(19,1),(20,0)} (SW). Correctly recolor the NE color1 shape to frame color6; preserve all else. Submission confirmed correct. This extends the frame-direction rule to west+south arms and confirms target is in the diagonal quadrant opposite both arms.

Additional confirmed recurrence (13x21, background 6): a large color-1 L frame has elbow (9,3), arms west and south (row 9, columns 0-3; column 3, rows 9-12). Two identical horizontal 2-cell bars lie in opposite diagonal quadrants: color 9 at {(5,16),(5,17)} in the NE/open quadrant, and color 8 at {(12,0),(12,1)} in SW. Recolor the NE color-9 bar to frame color 1; leave the SW color-8 bar unchanged. A separate 9 singleton, a 7 singleton, a color-4 7-cell shape, and a color-0 2x2 square are decoys and remain unchanged. Submission confirmed correct. This reinforces that long L frame color is destination and the matched copy in the quadrant opposite both arms is selected.


Additional confirmed 24x12 recurrence: bg3; color0 thin L frame at column 8 rows0-8 plus row8 cols8-11 (arms north+east). The exact matching shapes are isolated singleton color4 at (7,5) and singleton color9 at (1,10), on opposite west/east sides of the vertical arm but both north of the horizontal arm. Correct output recolors only the west singleton (4->0); leave the color9 singleton, a color4 domino, and a large color2 block unchanged. Changing the large color2 block to frame color was explicitly wrong. This clarifies that matching copies need not straddle both marker axes: when copies are west/east of the vertical arm, select the copy opposite the horizontal arm's direction (here west, as the arm points east). A demo with a color7 frame whose arms point east+south likewise selected the west copy of an exact matching pair both south of the horizontal arm. If matching copies also straddle the horizontal arm, the selected object is in the open diagonal quadrant, consistent with prior examples. Do not infer the target from large size or open-quadrant location alone; first identify the exact matching-shape pair.
", path='arc', scope='global', reference={}, arguments={}, metadata={}, source='agent', created_at='2026-10-21T06:00:01.829721+00:00', updated_at='2026-10-21T06:13:30.141945+00:00', version=7), HarnessEntry(id='arc_recolor_full_uniform_separator_lines', kind='memory', title='ARC recolor full uniform separator lines', content='In ARC grids with a noisy background and a second color appearing both as scattered cells and as full uniform rows/columns, inspect for complete straight lines of that second color.
